name: Congenital Bile Acid Synthesis Defect
aliases: Inborn Error of Bile Acid Metabolism

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Bile Acid Synthesis Defect

criteria.description: Detection of abnormal bile acid profiles in serum or urine by mass spectrometry
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes encoding bile acid synthesis enzymes (e.g., HSD3B7, AKR1D1)
Presence of neonatal cholestasis with normal or low serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT)
Histological evidence of cholestasis and giant cell hepatitis on liver biopsy
Improvement of clinical and biochemical parameters after bile acid replacement therapy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of abnormal bile acid profile plus either genetic confirmation or characteristic clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent progressive liver damage and liver failure.

laboratory: Abnormal bile acid profile with atypical bile acid intermediates detected by mass spectrometry
Normal or low serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) despite cholestasis
Coagulopathy with prolonged prothrombin time due to vitamin K deficiency
imaging: Ultrasound showing hepatomegaly and possible liver fibrosis
Liver biopsy demonstrating giant cell hepatitis and cholestasis
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as HSD3B7, AKR1D1, or other bile acid synthesis enzyme genes
other: Clinical improvement following bile acid replacement therapy (e.g., cholic acid)

distinguishingFeatures: Onset may be later in infancy or childhood
Presence of alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency on serum testing
Characteristic PAS-positive globules on liver biopsy

redFlags: Persistent neonatal cholestasis with normal or low GGT
Rapid progression to liver failure in infancy
Poor response to conventional cholestasis treatments without bile acid replacement
